build.reason: The recipe configures a static CMake build, and CMake includes the tokener source in the library linked by the target. This is a static recipe assessment, not a claimed build result.

input.reason: The entry passes fuzzer bytes and their length directly to the parser, whose interface accepts an explicit length. This foundation supports single-call inputs; the missing incremental route is assessed as a coverage blocker.

lifecycle.reason: The target creates one tokener, releases the returned object, then frees the tokener. The source returns an owned result on success and accepts a null object in json_object_put.

control_flow.reason: The entry's call reaches number parsing for numeric bytes, including changed exponent handling, then returns to its cleanup path. Its one-call route and default flags limit coverage as reported in the blockers.

accepted.requirement: Exercise supported incremental number parsing across calls to json_tokener_parse_ex on the same tokener.
accepted.target_route: LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput creates a tokener, passes the entire fuzzer buffer to one json_tokener_parse_ex call, then frees the tokener.
accepted.failure_condition: No input can make the target resume a saved exponent on a second call, so the g0003 state reconstruction is unreachable.
accepted.alternative_paths: A single input can parse the same completed number, but cannot exercise restoration from previously saved tokener state; there is no second call or helper route.

source_evidence.quote:
/*  Check a basic incremental parse */
    {"{ \"foo", -1, -1, json_tokener_continue, 0},
    {"\": {\"bar", -1, -1, json_tokener_continue, 0},
    {"\":13}}", -1, -1, json_tokener_success, 1},

accepted.requirement: Make the parser's supported strict-mode treatment of incomplete exponents reachable under the target's parse_ex operation.
accepted.target_route: The target uses json_tokener_new and calls json_tokener_parse_ex without setting flags; the constructor zero-initializes tokener state.
accepted.failure_condition: Inputs such as "[0e]" always follow the default-mode trimming route; strict-mode rejection cannot be selected by any fuzzer bytes.
accepted.alternative_paths: Default-mode parsing is not equivalent to strict-mode rejection, and the complete target has no flag setter or alternate tokener construction route.
